title: How quickly would a 60-tonne xenon detector confirm or exclude the LZ high-energy hint?
question: For LZ-like (E50 = 270 keV) and extended (300/400/600 keV) ROIs, the present generation (LZ + XENONnT + PandaX-4T) and a 40-60 t detector from ~2032, what exposure gives 5 sigma on the LZ best-fit L10 and inelastic (delta = 300/350/366/380 keV) rates, zero-event exclusion of the LZ 90% lower edge (0.105-0.38 per 2.84 t yr), 3 sigma L10-vs-inelastic-366 shape separation, and delta to +-10 keV from the xenon spectrum, with MSSI scaled as surface/volume?
headline_result: A 60 t detector with a 400 keV ROI reaches 5 sigma on LZ's best-fit rate after 8.5/9.6/3.6/1.1/0.13 t yr (L10/300/350/366/380 keV; 1 day to 2.5 months live), excludes the 0.105 lower edge with 49 t yr (one year) and separates L10 from inelastic-366 with 4-6 events; detector size changes exposures by only 1-2% because the band above 200 keV holds <= 1e-3 background events per 2.84 t yr, so the hint is exposure-, not background-limited, and the present generation with an LZ-like ROI reaches 5 sigma at the best fit by 2027-2028 (never at the lower 68% rate)
key_numbers: acceptance LZ/400 keV edge L10 0.42/0.54, d300 0.81/0.93, d350 0.44/0.87, d366 0.17/0.83, d380 0.028/0.83; 400 keV rates 0.45/0.40/0.69/1.70/10.5 per t yr; bkg >200 keV per 2.84 t yr LZ window 6.0e-4 (5.0e-4 at 60 t), 400 keV 2.7e-3 (1.6e-3); surface scale 0.49 (60 t) 0.56 (40 t); E5sigma LZ window 12.3/11.5/8.5/6.8/5.7, 400 keV 60 t 8.5/9.6/3.6/1.08/0.13 (x4.6 at x0.30), 600 keV 6.4/9.5/3.4/0.97/0.12; 5 sigma = 2.0-4.0 events; E90 zero events (0.105/0.38): LZ window 62/17 (95%: 81/22), 400 keV L10 49/13.6, d350 32/8.8, d366 12.9/3.6, d380 2.1/0.58; LZ alone 5 sigma 2027.65 (L10), present gen 2026.7 with reanalysed XENONnT/PandaX; L10 vs d366: 25% of L10 outside 167-437 keV support, N3sigma 4 (L10 true)/6 (inel true) at 400 keV, 10 in LZ window, KL 1.46/0.89 nats; delta: sigma per event 23/19/27 keV at 350/366/380, N(+-10 keV) 5.2/3.8/7.3 -> 7.6/2.2/0.69 t yr, endpoint <= 4% of information, halo +-16 keV, W/Xe ratio ~4 events per target
model_or_mechanism: WimPyDD O1 isoscalar inelastic (1 TeV) and L10 dipole-dipole spectra normalised to one LZ-ROI event; erf efficiency windows + sqrt(E) resolution; binned NR-band background with per-tonne-constant and 1/R surface parts; binned Asimov significance; CLs zero-event limits; support-counting and toy LLR shape tests; Fisher information on delta
result_type: computed (spectra, acceptances, Z, exclusion, Fisher, toys) / estimated (extension backgrounds, detector parameters, calendar)
confidence: medium - rates and acceptances validated against P012/P038 to 1-3%; exposures rest on recalled detector parameters (XLZD 40-60 t from 2032, fiducial masses, live fractions) and the LZ rate band; Asimov Z asymptotic (<= 15% on exposures)
agent_tools: Read x22, Bash x19, Write x5, Edit x20, Skill x1 (dataviz)
software_and_packages: python 3.12.13; WimPyDD 2.0.4 (eft_hamiltonian incl. q-dependent L10, streamed_halo_function 12 days via lz.wd_halo, diff_rate via lz.wd_rate); numpy 2.5.3; scipy 1.18.1 (erf, norm, poisson, brentq); pandas 3.0.5; matplotlib 3.11.2; common/lzcommon.py
local_inputs: PAPER_GUIDE; dossier; ledger; papers P004/P005/P010/P012/P015/P020/P021/P022/P034/P035/P038; work/P038 acceptance + MSSI CSVs + details; work/P016 results.json; work/P034 derived_numbers; work/P020 exposure_scenarios; P012/P038 scripts; tex l.67/77/160-165/767; lzcommon.py; ENVIRONMENT_versions
